case_study_insert.main_stem: Xanadu Parcel Company (XPC) is a public limited company in the online gift retailing and e-commerce fulfilment sector, employing a workforce of 40. Founded in 2005 by Xanthe Xanadu, the business sells personalised gifts through its own website and packs orders for other retailers, operating a hierarchical structure with laissez-faire leadership. XPC plans to invest $810,000 in a new automated gift-wrapping and dispatch line, financed by a $510,000 ten-year bank loan and a $300,000 share issue. It has fixed costs of $216,000 a year, a variable cost of $12 a unit and a selling price of $21, and currently produces 66,000 units a year. XPC faces two problems: absenteeism is rising and gift-wrapping quality complaints have increased.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations and Marketing Report, Q3 2025: XPC packed 16,800 gift orders last quarter with a packing error rate of 2.7%, down from 4.4% last year. Customer complaints fell from 44 to 26 per month. Average dispatch time is 3.6 days. A survey of 500 online gift buyers found 62% would pay up to $1.20 more for recyclable packaging, and 55% check delivery speed before ordering. Records show 13 of 40 staff still need on-the-job training on the new wrapping line; off-the-job training courses at the local college cost $720 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Xanadu Parcel Company as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank raised the base interest rate from 4.0% to 4.9%, increasing borrowing costs on variable-rate business loans. (2) The national minimum wage rises by 5.5% from $13.60 to $14.35 an hour from April 2026. (3) Cardboard and courier input costs have risen 9.8% year on year, while online gift spending grew 3.8%.

questions.question_text: XPC plans to fund part of its automation with a ten-year bank loan. Explain two advantages for XPC of using a share issue to finance the expansion instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: A share issue raises $300,000 of equity that never needs repaying and carries no interest, unlike the $510,000 bank loan. With fixed costs of $216,000 a year and cardboard and courier costs up 9.8%, avoiding debt service protects cash flow and leaves more of the $21 selling price to absorb cost rises.

Point 2: Equity requires no collateral, so the $810,000 wrapping and dispatch line is not at risk of repossession if gift demand falls. It also strengthens the balance sheet of a public limited company answerable to shareholders before further borrowing. The 62% of 500 buyers who would pay $1.20 more for recyclable packaging give a growth chance that can be pursued without lender conditions.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of a share issue identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to XPC's costs, finance and survey evidence.

questions.question_text: XPC is promoting its recyclable packaging option for online gifts. Consider a national television campaign, search-engine advertising, or social media influencer marketing. Which should XPC choose to promote this option? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Television campaign: A national TV advert would build broad awareness of XPC's personalised gifts and could win new retail clients, but airtime is costly for a business funding an $810,000 line, and most viewers do not order gifts online, so much of the spend would be wasted.

Search-engine advertising: Paid search catches shoppers looking for personalised gifts or recyclable packaging, is measurable and can be budget-capped, protecting cash alongside the $510,000 loan. Its limitation is that it only captures existing demand and cannot create desire for the new packaging option among the 55% of 500 buyers who check delivery speed but may not know XPC's offer.

Social media influencer marketing: Gift and lifestyle influencers can demonstrate the recyclable packaging and the personalised products to a receptive audience, matching the 62% of buyers who would pay $1.20 more. It is targeted and measurable, though results depend on the influencer's credibility and may take time to build.

Recommendation: XPC should choose social media influencer marketing with a small search budget. It reaches online gift buyers, explains the $1.20 recyclable proposition and costs far less than television, which is rejected as unaffordable and untargeted. Search alone is rejected because it cannot generate the awareness needed to launch a new packaging option.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited description of promotional methods with minimal reference to XPC.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discussion of advantages and disadvantages of at least two methods applied to XPC's online gift business.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three methods with a justified recommendation that rejects television and explains the limits of search advertising.

questions.question_text: XPC's absenteeism is rising and gift-wrapping quality complaints have increased. Explain two benefits for XPC of using laissez-faire leadership to improve motivation in its fulfilment team.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Laissez-faire leadership lets the 40 staff decide how they organise wrapping and packing, which can raise job satisfaction and reduce the absenteeism that disrupts the 16,800 gift orders packed last quarter. In a flat approach to routines, experienced packers take ownership, helping cut the 2.7% packing error rate.

Point 2: Giving staff freedom to solve problems uses their close knowledge of the wrapping line, so quality faults behind the rising complaints are corrected quickly without waiting for approval. Autonomy makes the $720 college training more useful and supports the $810,000 automation while local teams adapt the new machinery.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of laissez-faire leadership identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to XPC's absenteeism, errors, structure and training.

questions.question_text: XPC must train 13 staff on the new gift-wrapping line. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the local college. Which should XPC choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Coaching beside the wrapping line is specific to XPC's machinery and quality standards, costs no fees, and keeps the 13 staff packing the 16,800 orders processed each quarter. It directly targets the 2.7% packing error rate and the quality complaints. Drawbacks are that the trainer's output falls, bad habits may spread, and no certificate is awarded.

Off-the-job training: College courses at $720 per employee cost $9,360 for the 13 staff, a small part of the $810,000 investment. They give structured skills and a recognised certificate, useful for a public limited company. However, staff are away from the line, lengthening the 3.6-day dispatch time, and generic content may not match XPC's wrapping machinery, so on-site follow-up would still be needed.

Decision: XPC should choose on-the-job training first, with short college updates later. It is cheaper, machine-specific and avoids losing output while absenteeism is rising and quality complaints remain. Full off-the-job training is rejected because $9,360 and the absence of 13 staff would slow the 3.6-day dispatch promise during automation, and laissez-faire leadership suits learning by doing on the line.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to XPC.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in XPC's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, disruption, quality and machine relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how XPC's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $216,000 ÷ ($21 − $12) = $216,000 ÷ $9 = 24,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 24,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $21 − $12 = $9.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $9.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways XPC's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare break-even output of 24,000 units with output of 66,000 units to show a margin of safety of 42,000 units, confirming the new line can run without losses.
2. Use the $1.20 premium that 62% of buyers accept to model contribution rising from $9.00 to $10.20, supporting the recyclable packaging decision.
3. Set volumes that cover $216,000 fixed costs and $510,000 loan repayments, checking the 66,000-unit plan can service debt.
4. Track unit cost ($216,000 ÷ 66,000 + $12 = $15.27) each quarter to benchmark the wrapping line and detect waste behind the 2.7% packing error rate.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 24,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $9.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety against 66,000-unit output; modelling the $1.20 recyclable premium; loan-service volume targets; and unit-cost benchmarking at $15.27 to monitor packing errors.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in each of (i) and (ii); 1 mark per valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate XPC's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has XPC's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.80 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.67 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 1.05 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 0.87 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $96,000 + $58,000 + $76,000 = $230,000; 2025 current assets = $112,000 + $70,000 + $52,000 = $234,000. For 2024, $230,000 ÷ $128,000 = 1.80; for 2025, $234,000 ÷ $140,000 = 1.67. Excluding stock: 2024 ($230,000 − $96,000) ÷ $128,000 = $134,000 ÷ $128,000 = 1.05; 2025 ($234,000 − $112,000) ÷ $140,000 = $122,000 ÷ $140,000 = 0.87.

Evaluation: Liquidity has weakened. Coverage of short-term obligations fell from 1.80 to 1.67 as current liabilities rose from $128,000 to $140,000 faster than current assets. The stock-excluding measure fell more sharply, from 1.05 to 0.87, so XPC now relies on selling inventory to meet short-term debts, a concern while it services a $510,000 loan and commits $810,000 to a new line. Cash fell from $76,000 to $52,000 and receivables rose from $58,000 to $70,000, tying up funds. The remaining coverage around 1.67 is still workable, so the position is not critical.

Conclusion: XPC's financial position has not improved. Both measures fell, and the stock-excluding measure dropping below 1 shows the decline is not merely an inventory effect. XPC should tighten credit control on the higher receivables and rebuild cash before further expansion.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations with detailed evaluation of inventory, receivables, cash and liabilities and a justified conclusion that the position has not improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for XPC of introducing recyclable packaging for its online gifts.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Recyclable packaging matches the 62% of 500 buyers who would pay up to $1.20 more, protecting the $9.00 contribution per unit as cardboard and courier costs rise 9.8%. It supports the $810,000 wrapping line and the 55% who compare delivery speed before ordering.

Disadvantage: Recyclable materials usually cost more than standard cardboard, raising the $12 variable cost per unit unless the full $1.20 premium is accepted. Any weaker protection could increase the 2.7% packing error rate and quality complaints, while the 3.6-day dispatch time must be maintained.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to XPC's survey data, costs and expansion.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 4.9%, the 5.5% minimum wage increase and the 9.8% rise in cardboard and courier costs will affect XPC. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.0% to 4.9%): If XPC's $510,000 ten-year bank loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost rises by 0.9% of $510,000 = $4,590 a year (0.009 × $510,000). This is small relative to fixed costs of $216,000, and if the loan is fixed-rate the direct cost is zero. Higher rates could dampen gift spending and raise future borrowing costs, but the exposure is limited and can be hedged.

Minimum wage increase (5.5%, to $14.35 an hour): With a workforce of 40, higher hourly pay raises XPC's wage bill and cannot be avoided. The insert gives no hours worked or individual wages, so an annual total cannot be invented; the defensible benchmark is productivity of 66,000 ÷ 40 = 1,650 units per worker. If productivity holds, the rise is manageable; if it falls, the $9.00 contribution per unit is squeezed.

Cardboard and courier inflation (9.8%): The $12 variable cost per unit is exposed, but the insert does not decompose it, so only an illustrative bound is honest: if the whole variable cost rose 9.8%, that adds 9.8% × $12 = $1.18 per unit, roughly $77,700 a year at 66,000 units. The $1.20 premium accepted by 62% of buyers can offset much of this.

Conclusion: The 9.8% rise in cardboard and courier costs has the greatest impact. It recurs on every unit, directly threatens the $9.00 contribution supporting the $810,000 line, and is only partly offset by pricing; the interest rise is modest and the wage effect depends on hours not stated in the insert.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to XPC.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on XPC's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three changes in XPC's context with a justified greatest-impact judgement that avoids invented figures.
